newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy seen selling marks as lira slips.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy seen selling marks as lira slips.

text.p: The Bank of Italy was seen selling marks around 999 lire, foreign exchange dealers said.
At 0928 GMT the lira was quoted at 1,000.30/0.80 per mark.
The central bank was earlier seen asking for prices above 998 lire per mark.
The lira had opened weaker and the Bank had asked for prices after the Italian currency sank through the 998 lire level.
"The Bank of Italy is keeping a close watch on the lira and intervened at 999.30 per mark," one dealer said.
Operators noted that Btp bond futures were also under pressure with the June Liffe contract off 84 basis points at 124.82 at 0937 GMT in a market nervous about an EMU delay.
"The lira for its part is easing on uncertainties over the Italian political scene, and the fact that the dollar is also weakening against the mark is not helping," one dealer said.
